chunks: The oppressors inherit it by (mutual) agreement!

The first of them serves as a leader for the latter one and the latter one follows the first one. They vie with each other in (the matter of) this lowly world, and leap over this stinking carcass. Shortly the follower will denounce his connection with the leader, and the leader with the follower. They will disunite on account of mutual [animosity] and curse one another when they meet.

Then after this there will appear another arouser of mischief who will destroy ruined things. The heart will become wavering after being normal, men will be misled after safety, desires will multiply and become diversified and views will become confused.
ai.seo_question: What characterizes the behavior and eventual downfall of oppressors according to Nahj al-Balagha?
ai.summary: Imam Ali (AS) illustrates the inevitable decay of unjust regimes, where power is inherited through temporary pacts that dissolve into mutual animosity as leaders prioritize fleeting worldly gains over spiritual integrity. This internal fragmentation precedes the 'shaking trial' (al-Fitnah al-Rajifah), a period of widespread doctrinal confusion and moral deviation that tests the steadfastness of the faithful. The passage serves as a prophetic warning about the cyclical nature of political corruption and its impact on societal cohesion.
